we have proposed two novel joint estimation algorithms for the CIR (channel impulse response) and the CFO (carrier frequency offset), for linear periodic channels, with high spectral efficiency and lower complexity compared to the conventional maximum likelihood estimator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for linear periodic channels, the joint estimation problem can be tackled with relatively low computational complexity by exploiting both approximate sparsity of the CIR and periodicity of the CIR.

the joint estimation problem can be solved with low computational complexity and high spectral efficiency, even in the absence of a-priori information about the sparsity pattern, by exploiting the periodicity and sparsity of the channel and noise.
